Head_and_Face: Eyes are small and positioned laterally with a distinctive reddish-orange iris.
Mouth is terminal with thick, fleshy lips.
Two pairs of short barbels are present at the mouth corners.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is deep, laterally compressed with an elongated oval silhouette.
Scales are minute and deeply embedded in thick, slimy skin giving a smooth, glossy texture.
Dorsal coloration is olive-green to golden-brown transitioning to lighter yellowish ventral surface.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Fins are rounded with soft rays.
Dorsal fin is short and positioned mid-body.
Caudal fin is truncate to slightly emarginate.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are large and positioned laterally; some varieties exhibit protruding telescope eyes.
Mouth is terminal and protractile with no barbels.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is laterally compressed and ovoid; proportions vary by breed from streamlined to egg-shaped.
Scales are cycloid and moderately large, arranged in regular overlapping rows creating a shimmering, reflective texture.
Domesticated varieties display vivid metallic orange, red, yellow, white, or calico patterns with iridescent scale surfaces.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Dorsal fin is single, elongated, and positioned mid-body.
Caudal fin varies from forked to double-tailed or fantail in domesticated varieties.
Anal and pelvic fins are paired and ventrally positioned.

Head_and_Face: Head is conical and blunt with a short, rounded snout.
Eyes are small, dark, and circular with no nictitating membrane.
Mouth is large and arcuate with 5-7 rows of triangular, serrated teeth.
Five gill slits are positioned laterally anterior to pectoral fins.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and torpedo-shaped (fusiform) adapted for sustained high-speed swimming.
Body exhibits countershading: dark grey to brownish-grey dorsal surface transitioning sharply to white ventral surface along the lateral midline.
Skin is covered in dermal denticles giving a rough, sandpaper-like texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Pectoral fins are large, broad, and wing-like.
First dorsal fin is tall and triangular, positioned mid-body.
Caudal fin is crescent-shaped (lunate) with a pronounced ventral notch.

Head_and_Face: Head is broad and blunt with a short, rounded snout.
Eyes are positioned laterally with a greenish hue and elliptical pupils.
Mouth is wide with distinctive teeth: upper teeth have deeply notched, curved cusps; lower teeth are narrower with serrated edges.
Five gill slits are positioned laterally.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is cylindrical anteriorly, becoming laterally compressed posteriorly.
Distinctive dark vertical bars or stripes on a grey to greenish-grey dorsal surface, fading to white ventrally.
Striped pattern is most prominent in juveniles and becomes less distinct with age.
Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough, abrasive texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: First dorsal fin is tall and positioned anteriorly.
Second dorsal fin is smaller and positioned near the caudal peduncle.
Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are small and positioned dorsally.
Spiracles (respiratory openings) are large and positioned immediately posterior to the eyes.
Mouth and nostrils are positioned ventrally.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is a distinctive circular to oval disc formed by expanded pectoral fins fused to the head and trunk.
Dorsal surface is smooth and naked with a soft, rubbery texture.
Coloration is typically uniform brown, grey, or reddish with no distinctive patterning.
Pair of large electric organs visible as kidney-shaped swellings on the dorsal surface behind the eyes.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tail is thick and muscular, shorter than the disc in most species.
Small caudal fin at the tail terminus.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are small and positioned dorsally.
Mouth and nostrils are positioned ventrally.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is a flattened, diamond-shaped to circular disc formed by expanded pectoral fins fused to the head and trunk.
Dorsal surface is smooth and naked with a soft, leathery texture.
Coloration varies from sandy brown to olive to dark grey, often with mottled or spotted patterning.
One or more venomous barbed spines positioned on the dorsal surface of the tail near the base.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Tail is long, thin, and whiplike, often exceeding disc length.
Pelvic fins are divided into anterior and posterior lobes.

Head_and_Face: Comb is a fleshy, serrated crest on the crown, bright red and vascularized.
Wattles are paired fleshy appendages hanging from the lower beak, bright red.
Beak is short, curved, and keratinous with a yellow to grey coloration.
Eyes are dark and positioned laterally.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact and robust.
Plumage is vivid and iridescent with metallic green, blue, purple, or copper tones on the neck, breast, and tail feathers.
Hackle feathers (neck plumage) are elongated, pointed, and glossy, forming a distinctive ruff.
Saddle feathers (lower back) are elongated and flowing.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are stout with thick, scaled skin and a prominent posterior spur on the tarsus.
Feet are anisodactyl (three toes forward, one backward) with sharp, curved claws.
Tail feathers are long, curved, and iridescent with a characteristic arching posture.

Head_and_Face: Comb is smaller and less developed than male, often pale red or pink.
Wattles are reduced or absent.
Beak is short, curved, and keratinous with a yellow to grey coloration.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is compact and rounded.
Plumage is cryptic with mottled brown, buff, grey, and black patterning.
Feathers lack the iridescent sheen of male plumage.
Hackle feathers are shorter and more rounded than male.
Abdomen is broader and more rounded than male.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are scaled with no or reduced spur development.
Feet are anisodactyl (three toes forward, one backward) with moderate claws.
Tail feathers are shorter and less curved.

Head_and_Face: Head is small relative to body with large, prominent eyes with long, dark eyelashes.
Beak is short, broad, and flattened with a blunt tip.
Neck is elongated, slender, and nearly featherless with pink to grey skin.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is massive and ovoid.
Male plumage is two-toned: black body feathers with white primary and secondary wing feathers and tail plumes.
Female plumage is uniform grey-brown.
Feathers are soft and fluffy with a loose, hair-like texture lacking interlocking barbules.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are extremely long and muscular with only two toes (didactyl) on each foot.
Large inner toe bears a thick, blunt claw; smaller outer toe is present.
Wings are small and vestigial, used for balance and display rather than flight.
